articles.title: Three Key Messages for Employers Managing Rising Healthcare Costs
articles.summary: Healthcare expert Katie Martin outlines critical strategies for self-funded employers grappling with escalating medical and pharmacy benefit expenses. The guidance emphasizes actionable plan design and cost-management approaches that directly impact commercial employer health plans.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Tue, 13 Oct 2026 22:27:25 GMT

articles.title: High Unit Prices Drive U.S. Employer Healthcare Spending
articles.summary: Expert analysis underscores that underlying unit prices—rather than just utilization—remain the primary driver of escalating healthcare costs for U.S. employers. For self-funded plans, this highlights the critical need for aggressive price containment strategies within pharmacy and medical benefits. The discussion emphasizes that managing cost trends requires tackling unit prices directly rather than focusing solely on utilization management.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Tue, 13 Oct 2026 20:32:25 GMT

articles.title: Employer-Sponsored Healthcare Cost Growth Driven Primarily by Price Increases
articles.summary: Recent analysis highlights that rising healthcare costs for U.S. employers are primarily driven by underlying price increases rather than utilization shifts. For self-funded plan sponsors, this underscores the critical need for aggressive pharmacy and medical cost containment strategies to combat inflationary pressures.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Tue, 13 Oct 2026 19:41:15 GMT

articles.title: U.S. Hospitals Sue Over Revised 340B Rebate Models
articles.summary: Hospital groups are challenging revised 340B drug manufacturer rebate and pricing models in federal court. This ongoing legal battle impacts the broader drug supply chain, contract pharmacy arrangements, and drug cost dynamics that affect employer-sponsored health plans.
articles.source_line: Source: NAVLIN DAILY; Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:10:12 GMT

articles.title: UCSF Study Links PBM Rebates to Opioid Manufacturers, Sparking Reform Calls
articles.summary: Researchers at UCSF have uncovered undisclosed financial ties between pharmacy benefit managers and opioid manufacturers tied to drug rebate structures. The findings add momentum to legislative efforts targeting PBM transparency and rebate practices, directly impacting self-funded employers seeking greater accountability in drug spend.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Daily; Tue, 13 Oct 2026 23:22:52 GMT

articles.title: Employer Health Plan Costs Projected to Rise 8.2% Amid Data Lags
articles.summary: Projected employer health plan costs are expected to climb 8.2%, driven by underlying cost pressures and delayed claims data visibility. This rising trend directly impacts self-funded employers seeking proactive pharmacy benefit management strategies to control escalating health benefit expenditures.
articles.source_line: Source: Human Resources Director; Tue, 13 Oct 2026 23:35:10 GMT

articles.title: Walmart Expands Zero-Cost Coverage for Insulin and GLP-1s for Employees
articles.summary: Walmart is offering certain GLP-1 medications and insulin at zero cost to its employees as part of its health plan benefits. This move highlights how major self-funded employers are strategically managing chronic conditions and wrestling with the surging costs of obesity drugs. For self-funded employers and PBMs, it underscores the ongoing competitive pressure to balance benefit generosity with escalating specialty drug spend.

articles.title: Walmart Expands Employee Health Benefits to Cover GLP-1s and Insulin at No Cost
articles.summary: Walmart is updating its employer-sponsored health plan to provide zero-cost coverage for GLP-1 weight-loss medications, insulin, and inhalers. This move highlights major self-funded employers aggressively tackling chronic disease and obesity costs despite escalating utilization pressures. For self-funded plans and PBMs, it underscores the ongoing strategic debate around managing high-cost specialty drugs versus long-term health outcomes.

articles.title: Formycon Files US Biosimilar for Keytruda
articles.summary: Formycon has submitted a US regulatory filing for a Keytruda biosimilar, representing a major milestone in oncology cost management. As high-cost specialty biologics face patent expirations, upcoming biosimilars offer self-funded employers significant opportunities to lower net specialty drug spend. PBMs will need to strategically update their formulary positioning and utilization management to drive adoption of these lower-cost alternatives.

articles.title: Walmart Expands Zero-Cost Drug Benefit for Eligible Employees
articles.summary: Walmart is introducing a benefit covering over 250 medications at zero cost for eligible employees, signaling a continued shift toward value-based plan design and chronic condition management. For self-funded employers and PBMs, this highlights innovative benefit strategies aimed at improving medication adherence and managing overall health plan spend.
articles.source_line: Source: Yahoo Finance; Tue, 13 Oct 2026 14:35:38 GMT

articles.title: Walmart to Provide Free GLP-1s and Insulin to Employees by 2027
articles.summary: Walmart announced plans to offer zero-copay coverage for popular diabetes and weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro, as well as insulin, to its U.S. employees starting in 2027. This landmark self-funded employer benefit move will put immense pressure on other large corporations to evaluate their own specialty drug coverage and cost-sharing strategies for GLP-1s.
articles.source_line: Source: BigGo Finance; Tue, 13 Oct 2026 18:29:00 GMT

articles.title: UnitedHealth Initiatives Focus on Prior Authorization and Pharmacy Transparency
articles.summary: Truist reports that UnitedHealth is advancing initiatives centered on prior authorizations and pharmacy transparency. This is significant for self-funded employers and PBMs navigating increasing regulatory scrutiny and employer demand for greater visibility into drug benefit operations.
